correctness.rationale: For any fixed \(\lambda>0\) the strictly convex polyhedral fused-lasso prox is locally affine, with a connected-component averaging derivative \(P_\pi\). For any constant-preserving averaging map, graph coarea proves its exact \(J_w\) operator seminorm equals the maximum over nontrivial cuts. Any connected partition is strictly realizable as a proximal active face by setting a block-constant output, signed saturated cross-block dual variables and zero internal variables; a spanning-tree divergence flow absorbs any small perturbation exactly. Therefore the maximum is attained as a ratio of two proximal outputs. The two-clique barbell witness has input cut weight one and output variation \(t(q-t)\), giving quadratic order. The unweighted universal upper bound follows from oscillation and |E|. All weights/normalizations/zero-denominator boundaries were checked. Exact rational checks cover 206 selected small connected partitions/weights and five barbell primal-dual witnesses; finite checks are corroboration.

originality.rationale: The 2010 generalized-lasso affine projection theorem is properly credited, and the 2016 graph BV results and 2018/19 graph ROF convex minimality paper were compared at the level of their mathematical implications. The complete all-graph sharp two-input graph-BV constant, realization of every connected partition in the data parameter, and explicit order-n-squared barbell sensitivity are not stated or implied by the material inspected. Exhaustive priority is not established; a hidden equivalent geometric formulation is possible.

value.rationale: The exact all-weighted-graph constant is a naturally motivated sharp stability invariant of the widely used fused-lasso/ROF denoiser, measured in the same total-variation penalty as the estimator. The finite formula is nontrivial because all connected plateau partitions must be shown realizable as active data faces. The barbell lower bound \(\lfloor q^2/4\rfloor\) establishes quadratic growth, contrasting with Euclidean nonexpansivity and single-input total-variation suppression. Its graph-order significance survives without polynomial-time evaluation or a precise universal leading coefficient.
